text:
maya: hey team — saw a sharp p95/p99 spike on hosted API around 11:02 UTC, looks correlated with queue depth. graphs in ops channel.

jason: saw that, investigating. which customer or tenant is it hitting?

maya: multiple tenants but heavy tail from tenant-42 (embedding batch jobs). p95 jumped from 180ms->1.6s, p99 to ~3.4s.

ops-bot: alert: hosted-api.p95 > 1s for 3m (link to dashboard)

vinh: pulling runtime metrics now — queue_depth_total spiked to ~1200, avg worker utilization up but CPU steal also rose. grabbing top pods.

anya: rolling perf profiler for the affected host group. starting 30s flame and kvcache stats.

jason: quick dump from the node: `top` showed process inferenced at 70% CPU but `steal` at 18%. dmesg has a bunch of VM pause events. here's `kubectl top node` snapshot:
```
NAME           CPU(cores)   CPU%   MEMORY(bytes)   MEMORY%
node-rt-11     14m          70%    34Gi            65%
node-rt-11     (steal=18%)
```

maya: steal=18% is new. any noisy neighbor on that host?

vinh: found a cron process `tenant-42-db-snapshot` running on the same node within the same tenant's node pool — it spikes CPU during snapshot. it also holds a lock that prevents eviction of some sidecars.

anya: profiler shows kernel-selector falling back to cpu-path for a subset of inference tasks when GPU queueing reaches threshold, which increases per-token time. also KV cache hitrate dropped from 92%->64% around the same time (evictions up).

jason: so two simultaneous things: (1) CPU steal from snapshot job causing kubelet scheduling jitter and some containers losing GPU availability windows, (2) KV cache churn due to high-cardinality short requests from embeddings workload causing more kernel switches. compounded latency.

maya: exact logs from runtime metrics: `kernel_selector.mode_switches: 480` and `kernel_selector.fallback_cpu_count: 120` over 5m. batch latency tail increased.

vinh: reproduced locally with a synthetic workload: flooding with many short-context embedding requests + a CPU background load triggers kernel selector thresholds -> fallback. code snippet I used:
```
for i in range(1000):
  curl -s -X POST https://hosted.api/generate -d '{"model":"open-embed-7b","input":"short"}' &
```

maya: good repro. next steps? we need immediate mitigation for hosted to restore p95s.

jason: mitigation options:
- throttle per-tenant qps for tenant-42 (fast)
- cordon node-rt-11 so backups don't run there (requires infra change)
- tweak kernel-selector to be more conservative about CPU fallback (risky)
- increase KV cache size for the pool to reduce eviction (medium effort)

anya: recommend short-term: apply per-tenant soft rate limit + evict backup job from inference node pool. then monitor queue depth.

maya: I've applied a soft qps cap (50rps) for tenant-42 via rate-engine; pushing a request to infra to move the snapshot job off the inference pool.

deploy-bot: rolling config change: rate-limit tenant-42 -> 50rps (change id cfg-8891)

vinh: applied change and patched node taints so snapshot cron won't schedule on inference nodes. observing metrics...

maya: queue depth dropping, p95 back down to ~220ms, p99 ~420ms after 90s. KV cache hitrate climbing back to ~88%.

jason: good. what's root cause writeup for postmortem? summary draft: "concurrent tenant-originated CPU-heavy snapshot cron + high-cardinality short embedding workload caused KV cache churn and triggered kernel-selector to fallback to CPU path for many inferences, producing P95/P99 latency spike."

anya: add remediation actions: enforce tenant isolation for cron jobs (scheduling constraints), add kernel-selector hysteresis so short spikes don't flip to CPU fallback immediately, and add KV cache auto-scaling per pool.

maya: agreed. I'll create a follow-up RFC for kernel-selector hysteresis and KV cache auto-scale. jason, can you own tenant scheduling guardrail PR?

jason: on it, will open PR and include a canary.

vinh: i'll add a perf test that runs short-context embedding blast + background cpu steal to ensure hysteresis doesn't regress.

maya: thanks all — marking incident resolved for now. will keep monitoring for 2h. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: incident resolved (id: INC-2026-324).
